criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission coral reef/ocean monitoring with fluid lensing clearly stated, rationale with bleaching stats and references, single spacecraft justification, users/operators identified. Addresses all requirements with detail and citations.

evidence.quote: fluid lensing has been used in combination with AI analysis to detect colour/tone changes to the seafloor
Only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity in communications
would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Launch site/vehicle justified, SSO orbit characteristics, COE table, inclination vs altitude plot, STK 3D views and ground tracks, access report, EOL drag sail discussed. High understanding but some errors: RAAN description, circular orbit argument of latitude explanation, heavy reliance on Wikipedia timeline.

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusion summarizes key design decisions across launch, orbit, ground station, EOL and notes risk of Vega E availability and future expansion, derived from evidence.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet
A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Structure with executive summary, intro, body, conclusion present and readable, but figure/table labeling inconsistent, STK images lack proper numbers/titles, references are bare URLs and include Wikipedia which brief prohibits, inconsistent formatting.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Uses argument of latitude u=0 to replace undefined ω and ν but still lists classic elements incompletely; RAAN initial value equated to launch facility location incorrectly.
Claims launch from Kourou at 5.05°N allows two daily windows because latitude smaller than inclination – oversimplified, ignores launch azimuth and performance.
Swath requirement discussion omits sensor FOV calculation; 600 km altitude selection not quantitatively justified against 250 km reef width.

overall: Solid preliminary SSO mission for reef monitoring with good STK support and rationale, but report presentation and referencing weak, and some orbital mechanics explanations imprecise.

feedback.summary: You delivered a solid SSO reef-monitoring concept with clear purpose, users, and STK evidence. Your single-satellite rationale, 600 km SSO design, Vega E / Kourou selection, and Mt Pleasant access analysis show strong understanding. To improve, tighten orbital mechanics explanations, quantify swath vs reef width, and lift presentation to professional standard with proper figure labels and referencing.
next_steps: In Orbit section, fix COE definitions: explicitly note ω and ν undefined for circular e=0 orbits, define argument of latitude u correctly, and justify RAAN separately from launch site longitude with azimuth explanation.
Add quantitative justification for 600 km altitude: calculate required sensor FOV / swath to cover 250 km reef width and link to your STK ground-track screenshots.

For report presentation, number and title all STK images (e.g., Image 1, Image 4), make formatting consistent, and replace bare URLs/Wikipedia in Bibliography with proper cited sources as required by the brief.

criteria.C1: You addressed all intro requirements well. Primary mission using fluid lensing + AI for reef monitoring, bleaching rationale with references, single-spacecraft simplicity, and users like CSIRO/BOM were clear in Introduction. To stay high in Accomplished, add more specific literature depth.
criteria.C2: Strong design in Launch and Orbit: Vega E justification, inclination vs altitude plot, COE table, and Ground Control access report. Next level needs precise explanations - correct RAAN vs facility location, launch window vs azimuth, and add FOV swath calc to justify 600 km.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion effectively summarizes decisions from Launch, Orbit, Ground Control & Communications, and EOL drag sail, plus risks like Vega E availability. To strengthen, draw more explicit quantitative conclusions from your STK results.
criteria.C4: You have clear structure with Executive Summary and readable writing. To reach Accomplished, fix inconsistent figure/table labels in Mission Design, add proper captions to STK views, and format Bibliography with in-text citations - avoid bare URLs and Wikipedia.
